conclusion: Do not adopt the blanket prepared-update outer guard. Four public-behavior scenarios change in both lock families, including a newly detectable DB/metadata lock cycle through a public connection override. Production locks remain unchanged.
failure_classification: Complete valid observations and passed existing regressions; the unqualified adoption gate intentionally rejects detected behavior changes/deadlocks.

callback.notification: single background-process completion callback; REST polling internally

candidate: Existing DB guard spans complete JDBC3PreparedStatement.executeLargeUpdate body, including precondition checks; executeUpdate delegates. No other entrypoint widened.

summary.semantics: Observable scope changes block an unqualified equivalence claim; not every ordering difference is a JDBC specification violation. Primitive changes and pre-existing failures are separate findings.

environment.purpose: Scope behavioral equivalence gate, not a throughput test

scope_provenance.candidate: Existing DB guard spans complete JDBC3PreparedStatement.executeLargeUpdate body, including precondition checks; executeUpdate delegates. No other entrypoint widened.

methodology: Exact generated executeLargeUpdate body guard is exercised through real public JDBC calls; executeUpdate delegates. Other entrypoints are not widened.
Four classpaths separate monitor/ReentrantLock selection from original/coarse scope. Native binary is identical within each normal/fault stage.
Fresh JVM per scenario; rendezvous gates and bounded futures; no assertion of BLOCKED versus WAITING implementation state.
Metadata cycles use platform threads so ThreadMXBean can identify monitor/ownable-lock cycles; callback/cancel/transaction probes also use virtual threads.
One pre-existing transaction regression removed its Thread.State.BLOCKED-specific orchestration; final rollback/data assertions remain intact.

Early invalid probes assumed fatal UDF/READONLY statements remained reusable; source DB.execute finalizes these errors. Final probes record reuse behavior and separately validate recovery with a fresh prepared statement.
interpretation_limits: No claim that every observable ordering/latency change violates the JDBC specification.
New deadlock requires a public JDBC4Connection subclass override that queries metadata plus a concurrent metadata caller; not a claim that default JDBC callers always deadlock.
External DB/Connection monitor coordination loss is a primitive-migration difference, not a new outer-scope regression.
Timeout configuration/native-policy divergence and fatal-error statement invalidation were observed on original scope too; not caused by coarsening.

This is not proof of all JDBC methods, all interleavings, all native lifetime races, or all JDK/Android runtimes. Native timed-busy cancellation is not equated with the deliberately gated custom-handler cases.
Seven pre-existing disabled tests remain disabled; two normal-library fault-only skips were exercised in the separate fault stage.
